candidates.attacker_control: XML content is fully controlled by the party supplying it. For the XLS classes, an 'XML Spreadsheet 2003' spreadsheet (.xls/.xml document) passed to the public utilities API (XLSXmlParser(InputStream,name) / XLSXmlNormaliser(source).go()); these classes are shipped in the published org.hl7.fhir.utilities artifact and are used by downstream spreadsheet-to-FHIR tooling (HL7 IG-publisher ecosystem). For the DSTU2 parser, any DSTU2 XML resource handed to org.hl7.fhir.dstu2.formats.XmlParser.parse(InputStream) - reachable in-repo from the validator's VersionConvertor.convertVersionNativeR2 XML branch (org.hl7.fhir.validation .../VersionConvertor.java:25), from org.hl7.fhir.convertors loaders (XVersionLoader.java:24, VersionConversionService.java:102) and, for downstream users, from HAPI FHIR DSTU2 endpoints.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified against source: both XLS parseXml methods (167-176, 217-222) contain no factory hardening, and the DSTU2 file (206-238) lacks both the FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL setting and the DOCDECL rejection that all five sibling modules contain (grep for FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL and 'DTD declarations are not allowed' returns only the five siblings). No repository tests exercise DOCTYPE/XXE (searches for DOCTYPE/XXE/DTD in src/test returned nothing). Searched in-repo callers of XLSXmlParser / new XLSXmlNormaliser: none, so XLS impact requires a downstream consumer. Did not execute code or verify classpath-dependent XmlPullParser behaviour; no claim of runtime confirmation.
candidates.impact: Improper restriction of XML external entities: parsing attacker-supplied XML can disclose local files (content substituted into parsed cell/text values, and re-serialized by XLSXmlNormaliser), cause server-side requests/outbound connections via external entity/DTD references, and enable entity-expansion denial of service. For DSTU2 the exposure applies to any process that parses DSTU2 XML (validator/convertor CLI and downstream HAPI DSTU2 servers); for the XLS classes it applies to downstream tooling that consumes the published utilities API.
candidates.prerequisites: XLS classes: any caller that parses an untrusted spreadsheet with these public APIs (no call site exists inside this snapshot, so exploitation depends on a downstream consumer). DSTU2: the concrete XmlPullParser implementation on the classpath must process the DOCTYPE (xpp3 is a declared optional dependency of org.hl7.fhir.dstu2; kxml2 may be used in HAPI deployments). The five sibling modules show the maintainers consider DTD processing undesirable, and they block it from the caller side in exactly this way.
candidates.root_cause: One root cause: XML parser instances are created with DTD processing / external-entity resolution left enabled, i.e. the project's own XXE hardening was not applied everywhere. (a) XLSXmlParser.parseXml and XLSXmlNormaliser.parseXml call DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance(), set only setNamespaceAware(true) and pass the caller's InputStream straight to builder.parse(), so JDK/Xerces defaults (DOCTYPE allowed, external general/parameter entities and external DTD loading on) apply. (b) org.hl7.fhir.dstu2.formats.XmlParserBase.loadXml omits factory.setFeature(XmlPullParser.FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL, false) and its nextNoWhitespace silently skips XmlPullParser.DOCDECL events, whereas all five sibling modules (dstu2016may, dstu3, r4, r4b, r5) set FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL=false (e.g. dstu2016may line 210) and throw 'DTD declarations are not allowed' on DOCDECL (dstu2016may lines 235-237; same code in dstu3/r4/r4b/r5).
candidates.title: Missing XXE/DTD hardening in XML parsing entry points: XLS spreadsheet parsers (XLSXmlParser, XLSXmlNormaliser) use a default DocumentBuilderFactory, and the DSTU2 format parser still processes DTD declarations unlike its five hardened sibling modules
candidates.trace: XLS: XLSXmlParser(InputStream,name) (line 156) -> parseXml (167) -> DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() with no disallow-doctype-decl / external-*-entities / XInclude settings -> builder.parse(in) (172); a DOCTYPE declaring an external entity and a matching &entity; reference in cell/sheet content is expanded into the DOM whose cell values are returned by getColumn*/getRows, and XLSXmlNormaliser can write the expanded content back out via go() -> saveXml. DSTU2: XmlParser (extends XmlParserBase) constructor flow -> parse(InputStream) (XmlParserBase.java:115/125) -> loadXml(InputStream) (206) -> XmlPullParserFactory.newPullParser(); no FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL=false and no DOCDECL rejection in nextNoWhitespace (227-238), whereas the identical sibling implementations reject DOCDECL.
candidates.unverified: Not executed or runtime-confirmed. For the DSTU2 parser it is unresolved whether the XmlPullParser implementation in a given deployment resolves external entities (full XXE) or only processes internal DTD entities (DoS); the sibling-module hardening and the explicit 'DTD declarations are not allowed' message are indirect but strong evidence of the intended protection. Which of the two reported instances (XLS spreadsheet parsers vs DSTU2 parser) corresponds to a particular external advisory could not be verified from source alone; both are presented as instances of the same missing-hardening root cause. Other less clear-cut unhardened DOM parsers (XMLUtil.parseToDom* in org.hl7.fhir.utilities.xml, TranslatorXml.load, dstu2 utils/Translations) were not included as locations.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE); DTD/entity processing also exposes CWE-776-style entity-expansion DoS

coverage_summary: Read the repository inventory (7,227 files, 7,170 Java) and inspected the primary attack-surface modules in depth: org.hl7.fhir.utilities (XML/XHTML/JSON parsers, npm/package cache, zip/tar handling, HTTP/TLS), org.hl7.fhir.validation (loader/scanner/validators), org.hl7.fhir.convertors loaders, and the per-version format parsers (dstu2, dstu2016may, dstu3, r4, r4b, r5). The P1 relation index was used only for navigation (syntax-level call/containment/name candidates; explicitly not SAST, no data flow or reachability proof). The generated model classes and most non-parsing transform/renderer code were sampled, not read line-by-line.
limitations: P1 index coverage is partial: 7,224 of 7,227 source files indexed, only 612 files fully parsed, 10 parse errors, 3 source files missing from the index, semantic resolution/data-flow/control-flow not implemented, and 950,991 calls unresolved - index facts were treated as navigation hints only.
No code, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were executed; no runtime confirmation of any finding, and classpath-dependent XmlPullParser/certificate behaviour could not be exercised.
The snapshot's large generated model/code-system files were not exhaustively reviewed; only parser/loader/IO boundary code was traced closely.
Only one candidate may be submitted, so several plausible but weaker leads were recorded as rejected rather than fully validated.

External advisory/CVE identifiers, fix commits and sibling-repo data were intentionally not consulted, so the mapping of this source state to a specific known vulnerability could not be confirmed from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Trust-all TLS: SSLCertTruster.trustAllHosts() (org.hl7.fhir.utilities/src/main/java/org/hl7/fhir/utilities/npm/SSLCertTruster.java:31-53, X509TrustManager accepts everything; DO_NOT_VERIFY hostname verifier) is invoked via SimpleHTTPClient.trustAllhosts() (SimpleHTTPClient.java:115-118) from FilesystemPackageCacheManager.loadFromBuildServer() (~line 687), which installs an all-trusting SSLSocketFactory globally for the JVM (HttpsURLConnection.setDefaultSSLSocketFactory).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine CWE-295 weakness, but it is an explicitly documented, long-standing workaround in the code ('temporary fix... If this is still in the code in 2021, contact markiantorno'), used only for the build-server package list, so it is a hardening/design decision rather than the clearest specific candidate; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-slip containment check in TerminologyCacheManager.unzip (org.hl7.fhir.r4b and org.hl7.fhir.r5 .../terminologies/TerminologyCacheManager.java:97-114) compares a normalized absolute path String against targetDir with String.startsWith (line 102), which can be satisfied by a sibling prefix (e.g. .../txcache-evil vs .../txcache), while the archive is downloaded from a configured cache source in fillCache().
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible path-traversal-style bypass (CWE-22) but version-specific (r4b/r5 only), requires a malicious or compromised terminology-cache source, and the practical write region is limited to prefix-sibling paths; weaker and less certain than the XML-parsing candidate. The generic Utilities.unzip uses the correct Path-based containment check (Utilities.java:1506-1522).

rejected_leads.lead: Other unhardened XML parsers: XMLUtil.parseToDom/parseFileToDom (org.hl7.fhir.utilities .../xml/XMLUtil.java:436-470, called for example on a Measure attachment's data in org.hl7.fhir.validation .../instance/type/MeasureContext.java:34), TranslatorXml.load, and dstu2 utils/Translations.load use default DocumentBuilderFactory settings.
rejected_leads.reason: Same missing-hardening pattern (and XMLUtil is reachable when validating Measure attachments), but the classes have less clear-cut attacker control/impact than the reported instances and were left out to keep a single focused candidate; they are additional unconfirmed surface, not separately confirmed vulnerabilities.

rejected_leads.lead: Package-cache path construction from an unvalidated package id (FilesystemPackageCacheManager.addPackageToCache builds packRoot = Utilities.path(cacheFolder, id + "#" + v) at ~line 388 while only the version string is validated by checkValidVersionString at 205-217; Utilities.path itself resolves '..' components upward).
rejected_leads.reason: Would require a caller to pass a crafted package id that also matches the package.json name served by a package server, and the fetched package must then be installed; too many unverified preconditions to treat as the strongest candidate.

summary: Reviewed the 7,227-file snapshot (org.hl7.fhir.core 5.6.105 / HAPI 6.2.1), concentrating on XML/XLS/package parsing, zip/tar extraction, HTTP/TLS and validator entry points. Strongest source-supported issue: the repository's XXE hardening is incomplete — XML parsers still process DTDs/external entities. The clearest instances are the spreadsheet XML parsers in org.hl7.fhir.utilities.xls (default DocumentBuilderFactory) and the DSTU2 format parser, which is missing the DOCDECL rejection that all five sibling version modules carry. Impact is XXE (file disclosure, SSRF) and entity-expansion DoS when untrusted XML/spreadsheets are parsed. Other leads (jvm-wide trust-all TLS; a zip-slip containment check using String.startsWith; other unhardened DOM parsers) are noted as rejected/unconfirmed.
